summary: Wat Chedi Luang is a substantial working temple in the middle of Chiang Mai’s Old City, centered on the weathered remains of the city’s great historic chedi. The grounds also contain Lanna-style halls and naga sculptures, making this a rewarding architecture and history stop within a walking day.
whyGo: See the distinctive ruined brick chedi at close range in the heart of the Old City.
Compare the monumental stupa with the ornate Lanna ordination hall and other active temple buildings.
Combine easily with nearby Old City sights on foot.
bestFor: First-time Chiang Mai visitors interested in history and architecture
Travellers exploring the Old City on foot
Visitors who want a living temple as well as a historic monument
skipIf: You have already visited several similar temple compounds and want a different experience.
You need confirmed step-free access across the grounds.
You expect quiet or unrestricted access to every building during worship.
duration: Planning estimate: 45–90 minutes for the main compound; allow longer if you want to explore nearby Old City sights.
cost: The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s Japanese office lists admission at ฿50. Confirm the current charge at the entrance, since fees can change; transport and any guide are extra.
hours: Published hours conflict: the TAT Japanese office lists 08:00–22:00, while the Chiang Mai provincial tourism page lists daily 08:00–17:00. Confirm locally before planning an evening visit; access to individual buildings may differ.
bestTime: Go early for cooler weather and a calmer visit. Late afternoon can suit the light on the chedi, but verify closing time first.
gettingThere: At 103 Phra Pokklao Road in the central Old City. Walk from nearby accommodation or take a songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hailing car and specify Wat Chedi Luang. TAT Japan estimates 5–15 minutes from central Chiang Mai by songthaew; the actual time depends on traffic and pickup point.
booking: No advance booking is indicated for an ordinary visit. Pay at the entrance and check current access and any restrictions on arrival.
accessibility: Detailed step-free access, wheelchair routes and accessible toilet information were not found in the official listings. The historic compound has uneven surfaces and steps around some structures; contact the temple before travelling if access needs are specific.
practicalTips: Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where indicated and keep a respectful distance from worshippers.
Carry small cash for the entrance fee and any donation.
Ask before photographing people and follow signs about restricted areas.
Check which halls are open when you arrive; access can vary within the compound.
decemberNotes: December is a popular travel period and generally cooler than the hot season; allow flexibility for Old City crowds. This is seasonal planning guidance, not a December 2026 forecast. No specific December 2026 event or closure was verified.
uncertainties: Published official hours conflict (08:00–22:00 versus 08:00–17:00); confirm the closing time with the temple before a late visit.
The current entrance fee and access rules for individual buildings may change.
Detailed accessibility information and December 2026 exceptions were not available in the sources reviewed.
